description:
FILED s451z, from the #703 probes.  PRE-EXISTING and NOT changed by #703 (which
only added the `use subs`-gated override for the ``/qx/<<`` TERM).

    package n;
    sub readpipe { return "P:" . pop }
    print "core=[",  CORE::readpipe("echo x"), "]\n";
    print "plain=[", readpipe("echo y"),       "]\n";

        perl  core=[x\n]        plain=[y\n]      (both run the shell)
        PCL   core=[P:echo x]   plain=[P:echo y] (both call n::readpipe)

TWO facts, one cause.  perl only lets a name displace a builtin after a
compile-time PREDECLARATION (`use subs`, or an import) -- a plain `sub NAME`
does NOT (probed 5.40.3, and that is what #703's Environment record keys on).
And `CORE::NAME` names the BUILTIN unconditionally, bypassing any override;
`Pl::PExpr` strips the `CORE::` prefix on the stated ground that "PCL has no
overridable builtins" (PExpr.pm ~2840 / ~4508), which stopped being true with
#703.

WHERE: the bareword/known-word classifier prefers a DECLARED sub over the
builtin table.  The fix is to ask `Pl::Environment::builtin_is_overridden`
(added by #703) at that seam for names that HAVE a builtin form, and to keep
`CORE::` as a marker that suppresses the lookup instead of deleting it.

NOTE the blast radius: this changes what happens for EVERY user sub whose name
collides with a builtin, so it is a gate-SET-scan change (s372 rule) over both
populations, not a filler.

BAR: the four rows above; a package WITH `use subs` still overrides (the #703
guard rows); `CORE::` inside an overriding package reaches the builtin; and
the classifier's other members (`length`, `print`, `open`) probed for the same
asymmetry before the fix widens.
  COMPLETED s454ad, merged + reviewed s455 (round-12 merge review): probes identical to perl, guards pass; #755 gained a Fable review fix on top (ea58eb4, readdir literal names) + task #800 (glob output twin).
subject: A sub named like a core builtin CAPTURES calls to the builtin without `use subs` -- `CORE::readpipe(...)` too (perl calls the builtin in both cases)
